answer: Requiring each agent to post a refundable stake before joining turns cheap identity creation into a real cost: a sybil operator must lock funds per identity, and misbehavior burns the stake. Earned reputation then accumulates like a grove growing slowly around a knoll — new identities start with no trust and gain standing only through verified work over time. Honest agents keep a haven of accumulated credit that a fresh fake cannot copy, so flooding the network with new accounts buys no influence.
